memory_candidates.content: When computing a content digest over a file set that may be large (thousands of files), NEVER fork one subprocess per file (e.g. `git hash-object <path>` in a loop) and NEVER build the resulting fold text via bash per-element string concatenation (`list="${list}${x}"`) -- both degrade badly at scale (measured: ~2.2ms/file subprocess-fork overhead and ~9.7s for a 4815-entry concatenation loop alone). Instead, batch the hashing into one `git hash-object --stdin-paths` call (newline-separated paths on stdin, one hash per output line in input order) and build any prefixed/joined text via bash array parameter-expansion (`${arr[@]/#/prefix}`) or `paste -d TAB <(printf ...) <(printf ...)`, falling back to the slow-but-correct per-element path only on exit-code or count-mismatch irregularity, never trusting a partial batch result.

When multiple distinct call sites share an identical, expensive sub-computation keyed by a small set of inputs (e.g. several registry rows declaring the exact same corpus spec string), add a per-process memoization map (a `declare -gA` keyed by the joined input tuple, using a separator byte like \x1e unlikely to collide) rather than recomputing per call site. This is distinct from a cross-invocation cache/store: it costs nothing to add, has no staleness concern (it never outlives the process), and can turn an O(n_call_sites) cost into O(n_distinct_inputs) with a two-line guard at the top of the function.

git-commit-phase.sh's `--objective <id>` flag narrows commit derivation to exactly that one objective's own `files_touched` array in the phase's progress file; omitting the flag unions every objective in the phase (the correct form for a phase-closing commit). Passing a objective id that was never actually registered in the progress file's `objectives` array derives an EMPTY files_touched set, producing only a non-fatal 'nothing to derive' warning -- which is easy to misread as benign but actually means the real source diff was never staged, only the always-included task-directory pathspec landed. Always verify `git status`/`git diff --stat` on the specific files you intended to commit immediately after any `--objective`-scoped call, and prefer the bare (no `--objective`) form for any phase-closing commit.
